pr_title: Use the original canvas to calculate light positioning
pr_body:
#63101 is caused due to the ParallaxBackground's canvas layer transform being used to position lighting, rather than that of the original canvas layer the light is from. Because the ParallaxBackground transform is fixed in place without regard to the camera (unless `follow_viewport_enabled` is on), this causes the light's position on its canvas layer to be misaligned.

This commit fixes this for the general case (including other canvas layers such as UI) by fixing the canvas layer whose transform is used to calculate the light's position to be the one the light is in. This way the light's appearance will be consistent across all canvas layers.

*Bugsquad edit:* Fixes #63101
pr_comments: Should fix this for 4.0. Reviews are welcome.

issue_context.title: Wrong PointLight2D position on parallax layers when camera is active
issue_context.body: ### Godot version v4.0.alpha12.official [2c11e6d9e] ### System information macOS, Linux and Windows 10 ### Issue description The PointLight2D position on parallax layers is off when a camera is active. In my example, a flashlight is attached to the player. When camera is disabled the light illuminate the parallax layer at the right position: When camera is enabled the light position is off: Video of the minimal reproduction project: https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1422403/179389256-7b54426c-4857-4525-87da-0ed712e618e9.mov ### Steps to reproduce How to use the minimal reproduction project: - 'arrows' to move player - 'enter' to toggle on/off the camera ### Minimal reproduction project [parallax-light2d-camera-bug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9127203/parallax-light2d-camera-bug.zip)
comments: Can you reproduce this with the same setup on 3.4.4?

@Calinou on 3.4.4 it works correctly.

I found this issue while porting a project from 3.4 to 4.0

review_comments: There seems to be the same code in the OpenGL renderer in `drivers/gles3/rasterizer_canvas_gles3.cpp`, so I assume this needs to be changed too.
Yup, thanks for the heads-up. Compatibility mode works as well now too
